title: How do dew and frost form overnight?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Where does morning dew come from?
Why is the grass wet in the morning?
Why is my car covered in frost?

explain.say: On a clear night, grass and car roofs lose heat to the sky and cool down fast, often becoming colder than the air above them.

draw.text: How do dew and frost form overnight?

explain.say: After sunset there is no sunshine to replace the heat, and with no clouds acting like a blanket the surface keeps cooling. Calm air helps, because wind would stir in warmer air.
When the surface cools to the dew point, water vapour in the air touching it condenses into droplets: dew. Nothing falls from the sky; the water comes straight out of the air.
If the surface is below freezing, vapour turns straight into delicate ice crystals instead: frost. This change from gas straight to solid is called deposition.

faq.q: Does dew fall from the sky?
faq.a: No. Dew forms right where you find it. Water vapour in the air condenses onto cold surfaces like grass, just as droplets form on a cold glass of water.

faq.q: Why is there no dew on cloudy nights?
faq.a: Clouds act like a blanket, sending heat back down to the ground. The ground stays too warm to reach the dew point, so dew and frost rarely form.
asks: Why do clear nights get so cold?

faq.a: Frost is ice crystals that form when water vapour turns straight into ice on a surface colder than 0 degrees Celsius. Scientists call this deposition.

faq.q: Why does frost form on cars before roads?
faq.a: Car roofs and windscreens are thin and lose heat to the sky quickly, while roads store heat from the day. So car surfaces often cool below freezing first.
asks: Why is my car frosty in the morning?

faq.q: Why is dew heaviest on grass?
faq.a: Grass blades are thin and lose heat quickly, and they also give off water vapour. So they cool below the dew point fast with plenty of moisture around.
asks: Why is the grass wet in the morning?

facts: Frost forms by deposition, when water vapour turns straight into solid ice without first becoming liquid.
In the Namib Desert, fog and dew are a vital water source for plants and animals.

quiz.say: On which night is dew most likely to form?
quiz.why: Clear skies let the ground lose heat fast, and calm air lets the surface chill to its dew point.

wrong.0: Clouds keep the ground warm and wind mixes in warmer air, so the dew point is not reached.
wrong.2: Rain wets the grass, but that is rain, not dew; cloudy rainy nights stay too warm for dew to form.
